narrative.overview:
Swarm Arena is the category standard played straight: a Linear-grade dark dashboard, dense, quiet and precise. A cool near-black ground carries one raised panel tone, and structure comes from hairline borders rather than boxes, shadows or colour. The chrome is deliberately colourless (white, three greys, hairlines) so that the only saturated things on screen are the data: four track hues climbing a race chart, and the rare green or red of a verdict.

The system is dark only, by design. There is no light theme and no theme switch; `color-scheme: dark` is set at the root. Density is high and calm: 13-14px UI text, 10px row padding, 16px panel gutters, a 48px top bar. Nothing is decorative. Every saturated mark either identifies a track or reports a status, and every number is set in Geist Mono with tabular figures because it was measured, not written.

Motion is nearly absent. The one ambient animation is the pulsing live dot; everything else is a 150ms colour transition on hover. Reduced-motion collapses all animation and transition durations.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only: near-black ground (hue 265, a faint cool blue) with one raised panel tone and one hover tone.
Hairline structure: 1px `line` borders and `divide-y` rows; no card shadows.
Colourless chrome: the primary action colour is the foreground white.
Four categorical track hues, used only as data identity.
Status hues reserved for verdicts and always paired with an icon and a label.
Geist for UI, Geist Mono only for measured data.

rules.name: The Identity, Not Rank Rule
rules.body: Colour follows the entity, never its rank. A track's hue is fixed by its slot and never reassigned for leader, sort order or state; track hues never appear on chrome, buttons or text that is not about that track.

rules.name: The Reserved Status Rule
rules.body: Green and red mean verified and refuted, nothing else. They always ship with an icon and a label (Flag + "Finished", GitMerge + "Landed", CircleSlash + "Ruled dead"); colour alone never carries a status.

rules.name: The One White Rule
rules.body: The only action colour is the foreground white. Chrome stays greyscale so the data is the only saturated thing on screen.

rules.name: The Mono Means Measured Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is used only for data: Elo, moves and plies, counts, times, versions and seat IDs, always with tabular figures. Prose, labels and headings are never mono; a measured number is never sans.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: All labels, titles and badges are sentence case at normal tracking. Hierarchy comes from weight and the three ink tones, not from caps or letter-spacing.

rules.name: The Tonal Ladder Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by lightness step and hairline, never by shadow. A shadow appears only on something that floats above the page (tooltip) or on a pressed control.

dos: Do build every surface from the three-step tonal ladder (`bg`, `panel`, `panel-raised`) and 1px `line` hairlines.
Do give each track one series slot and use it for every mark about that track: line, dot, rung, filter, tooltip row.
Do pair every green or red with a lucide icon and a word, as the ladder's Flag + "Finished" and the feed's verdict rows do.
Do set every measured number in Geist Mono with tabular figures, and its label in sans `fg-3`.
Do direct-label chart series at the line end and keep an accessible table behind the chart.
Do keep transitions to 150ms colour changes and respect reduced motion.
donts: Don't add a light theme or theme toggle; the system is dark only.
Don't use a track hue for chrome, buttons, emphasis or decoration, or reassign hues by rank or leader.
Don't add a fifth categorical hue without re-running the CVD validator against `panel`.
Don't introduce a brand accent; the primary is white.
Don't put shadows on panels or rows; depth is tonal.
Don't set prose, headings or labels in mono, or numbers in sans.
Don't use uppercase or letter-spaced labels or eyebrow text above headings.
